name: Yasuo Hamanaka

summary.text: Yasuo Hamanaka was Sumitomo Corporation's chief copper trader. In June 1996 Sumitomo disclosed losses from his unauthorised trading, initially $1.8 billion and later $2.6 billion. In May 1998 Sumitomo settled CFTC charges that it manipulated copper prices in 1995-96 through LME trading, paying $150 million; Hamanaka admitted forgery and fraud charges in Tokyo and was sentenced to eight years in prison.

facts.claim: On 11 May 1998 the CFTC announced that Sumitomo Corporation, without admitting or denying the findings, consented to an order finding it had manipulated copper prices in 1995 and 1996 through LME trading, and agreed to pay a total of $150 million: a $125 million civil penalty paid immediately and $25 million placed in escrow for up to four years to fund restitution.

The page's statements on J.P. Morgan/Chase and UBS settlements ($125 million in 2002; about ¥10 billion) were not tested here.
